content: Bifidobacterium animalis is a Gram-positive, anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium that resides in the intestines of most mammals, including humans. It is one of the various species of bifidobacteria found in the human large intestine. Historically, Bifidobacterium animalis and Bifidobacterium lactis were classified as two separate species. However, they are now recognized as subspecies of Bifidobacterium animalis, specifically Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. animalis and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis. Despite this updated classification, the older names, B. animalis and B. lactis, are still commonly used on product labels, as this bacterium is widely utilized as a probiotic. In many cases, the specific subspecies included in a product is not explicitly identified. The strain Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis DN-173 010 is a widely used probiotic, particularly in the product Activia™, which is manufactured by the Danone company (known as Dannon in the United States). This strain is marketed under various trade names depending on the country. For example, it is called Bifidus Digestivum in the United Kingdom, Bifidus Regularis in the United States and Mexico, Bifidobacterium Lactis or B.L. Regularis in Canada, Bifidus Essensis in Germany, the Netherlands, Romania, and Austria, Bifidus Activo in Spain, and Bifidus Actiregularis in Argentina, Chile, Italy, and Russia. These trade names are not scientific but are designed to resemble scientific terminology. The accurate scientific name for this strain is Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis DN-173 010. Another commonly used strain is BB-12®, also referred to as Bb12 or Bb-12. This strain is incorporated into a variety of products worldwide, primarily dairy products but also dietary supplements such as capsules or pills. It is marketed by Chr. Hansen Ltd, a company based in Denmark. Similar to DN-173 010, BB-12® is often labeled as either Bifidobacterium animalis or Bifidobacterium lactis, but its precise scientific designation is Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis. Both DN-173 010 and BB-12® are extensively studied strains, and there is a substantial body of scientific literature supporting their efficacy. For instance, studies on BB-12® have demonstrated its effects on the intestinal microbiota of preterm infants, its ability to adhere to human intestinal mucus in both healthy infants and during rotavirus infections, and its role in activating transient pro-inflammatory responses in intestinal epithelial cells after colonization in germ-free rats. Similarly, research on DN-173 010 has shown that consuming fermented milk containing this strain can reduce oro-fecal gut transit time in elderly individuals. Additional studies have demonstrated that this strain shortens colonic transit time in healthy women and improves colonic transit time in healthy humans when consumed in fermented milk products. These findings highlight the potential health benefits of these probiotic strains in promoting gastrointestinal health.
